applies_why: The judge text decides whether the cited-in witnesses against C3 count as unanswered, which is the counting question K-G4 governs.
quote: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: The phrase 'pressed against' could mean either a verse merely appearing on a cited-in line or a verse whose pressing sentence is quoted from a named earlier round; I weighed both readings.
why: The judge asserts that every witness was pressed against C3 and then answers them from later rounds, but it never quotes any earlier pressing sentence or names the round where pressing occurred, as K-G4 requires before treating a verse as a witness, so the ground is resolved without the required quotation.
